draft.title: The effect of an outlier
card: An outlier is a value that is far from the rest of the data. For example, in the scores 6, 7, 7, 8, 9 and 40, the score 40 is an outlier.
An outlier pulls the mean towards it. Without the 40, the mean is \(\frac{37}{5} = 7.4\). With the 40, the mean is \(\frac{77}{6} \approx 12.8\).
An outlier changes the range a lot. The range is \(9 - 6 = 3\) without the 40, and \(40 - 6 = 34\) with it.
An outlier barely moves the median. The median is 7 without the 40, and \(\frac{7 + 8}{2} = 7.5\) with it.
draft.remember: An outlier pulls the mean and stretches the range, but the median hardly moves.

a.q: The ages of five friends are 12, 13, 13, 14 and 13. A 60 year old joins them. Which measure changes the least?
a.why: The median goes from 13 to 13, so it does not change at all. The mean jumps from 13 to about 20.8 and the range goes from 2 to 48. The mean is the tempting choice, but it is pulled towards the outlier.
a.clue: Find each measure before and after the 60 joins.

b.q: Leila's quiz marks are 14, 15, 15, 16 and 15. She then scores 2 on a sixth quiz. Which statement is correct?
opts: The mean falls by more than the median
The median falls by more than the mean
The mean and median fall by the same amount
The range stays the same as before
b.why: The mean goes from 15 to \(\frac{77}{6} \approx 12.8\), a fall of about 2.2. The median goes from 15 to 15, so it does not fall. The range grows from 2 to 14, so it does not stay the same.
b.clue: Work out the mean and median both before and after the 2.

b.best: The mean falls by more than the median

check.summary: No problems found. The card's working is correct (mean 7.4 to about 12.8, range 3 to 34, median 7 to 7.5), and both questions have exactly one right answer that matches the explanations.
